chunks: Amr ibn Saeed al-Madaini (who was a Fathi) narrated: I was with Abu al-Hasan al-Askari (peace be upon him) in Sayr when Ayyub ibn Nuh entered and stood before him. He ordered him something, then he left. Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) turned to me and said: O Amr, if you wish to see a man from the people of Paradise, look at this man.

key_terms.أَهْلِ الْجَنَّةِ: The people of Paradise, referring to those destined for Jannah.
key_terms.الْعَسْكَرِيِّ: Al-Askari, referring to Imam Ali al-Hadi (peace be upon him), the tenth Imam.
key_terms.بِصَيْرٍ: In Sayr (or Seville), a city in Syria (or Spain, depending on interpretation), here referring to the location of the event.
key_terms.فَطْحِيٌّ: A follower of the Fath sect, a group known for their belief in the hidden Imam's authority.

ai.seo_question: Who is Ayyub ibn Nuh and why did Imam al-Askari identify him as a resident of Paradise?
ai.summary: Amr ibn Saeed, a known narrator, witnessed Imam al-Askari (peace be upon him) designate Ayyub ibn Nuh as a resident of Paradise, illustrating the Shia concept of *al-ghayb* (occultation) and the spiritual authority of the Imams in recognizing the righteous. This incident underscores the Imam's ability to discern the inner state of individuals, affirming Ayyub's status among the *Ahl al-Bayt*'s close companions during the Minor Occultation.
